channel.title: Hospital Price Watch
channel.description: New issue briefs and research from the USC Center for Health Financing, Policy, and Management, and public appearances by Glenn Melnick.

item.title: Quoted in the news: UCLA Health expansion raises costs and concerns (Los Angeles Times)
item.description: Melnick, who has documented how hospital consolidation in Northern California raised costs, says mergers have continued in Southern California and that rising premiums leave employers little room for raises.

item.title: Media interview: California's billionaire tax promises healthcare relief. The fine print is murkier. (Marketplace (story credited to KFF Health News))
item.description: Glenn Melnick is quoted on how ballot measures are worded to win support and what that leaves open for how the money is used. Text story with an audio version.

item.title: Legislative testimony: Health Care Affordability in Minnesota: Trends and Challenges and Health Care Mergers (Minnesota Senate Health and Human Services Committee)
item.description: Committee briefing on health care mergers, drawing on the Sutter Health case study (Melnick and Fonkych, 2024): Sutter prices were similar to controls before systemwide contracting and about 30% higher afterward. Slides are public.

item.title: Radio interview: Skyrocketing Health Costs (Monks & Merrill, KFI AM 640 (iHeart))
item.description: On what family coverage costs workers: for someone earning $40,000 with employer family coverage, the premium share taken from the paycheck is close to $7,000 a year, the largest deduction from take-home pay.

item.title: Quoted in the news: Rising health insurance costs force Bay Area small businesses into tough choices (CBS San Francisco (KPIX))
item.description: On how premium growth holds down pay, and how hospital consolidation shifted bargaining power from health plans to hospitals.

item.title: Quoted in the news: California employer health premiums will cost as much as a new car in 2027 (Los Angeles Times)
item.description: On employer premiums passing the price of a new car, and large systems that can set the price they charge insurers.

item.title: Issue brief: The Outpatient Shift: Outpatient Care's Rising Share of California Hospital Revenue, 2014–2025
item.description: Across a fixed set of 248 general-acute hospitals, outpatient care's share of gross patient revenue rose from 35.8% in 2014 to 43.7% in 2024, and to about 45% in early 2025 filings. Rural hospitals now earn 68.5% of revenue from outpatient care, and the smallest hospitals 76.4%.

item.title: Research: Analysis of Hospital Trauma Center Charges for Commercially Insured Patients in the United States
item.description: Andreyeva, Yamamoto, Akintola & Melnick. Medical Care Research Review

item.title: Op-ed by Melnick: Bitter medicine: How California's hospital bills end up depressing your take-home pay (CalMatters Commentary)
item.description: Melnick argues that hospital prices feed employer premiums, which crowd out wage growth, and makes the case for California limits on cost growth.

item.title: Quoted in the news: A California county's only hospital cleared a federal hurdle, but it still needs millions to reopen (CalMatters (also in the Los Angeles Times))
item.description: On Glenn Medical Center: since a federal decision led to its closure, federal money for reopening would make sense; failing that, the state.

item.title: Research: Decomposition of trauma care prices between 2019 and 2022 in the US commercially insured population
item.description: Andreyeva, Koep, Advani, Melnick. Health Affairs Scholar

item.title: Research: Hospital Prices Post-COVID-19: Troubling Trends From California
item.description: Glenn Melnick. Health Affairs Forefront

item.title: Quoted in the news: Health Care Consolidation and Rising Costs Happen, but Obamacare Is Not the Key Culprit (KFF Health News)
item.description: On whether the Affordable Care Act drove hospital consolidation.

item.title: TV interview: Health premiums set to jump in 2026 (KTVU FOX 2)
item.description: Live interview before open enrollment on why premiums are rising about twice as fast as inflation and what workers and employers can expect.

item.title: Research: Hospital-Based Emergency and Trauma Care: The Expanding Epicenter of the US Healthcare Delivery System
item.description: Melnick et al. Healthcare (Basel)

item.title: Quoted in the news: Inside UCSF's $530 million gambit to save three struggling San Francisco hospitals (Gazetteer SF)
item.description: On UCSF's purchase of two Dignity Health hospitals and the risk of higher prices from shared market power.

item.title: Research: Are all-or-nothing contracts by hospital systems anti-competitive?
item.description: Melnick & Fonkych. Journal of Hospital Management and Health Policy (USC Schaeffer Center summary)

item.title: Q&A interview: Why some California hospitals are still struggling after COVID-19 (USC Price School)
item.description: Melnick explains how the pandemic disrupted hospital finances, why labor costs stayed high, and the case for the Office of Health Care Affordability, drawing on his Health Affairs Scholar study.

item.title: Research: Post-Covid Trends in Hospital Financial Performance: Updated Data from California
item.description: Melnick & Maerki. Health Affairs Blog

item.title: Quoted in the news: Hospital closures, cuts in services loom for some communities. How the state may step in to help. (CalMatters)
item.description: On the state emergency loan program for distressed hospitals.

item.title: Research: COVID-19 driven decline in emergency visits: Has it continued, is it permanent, and what does it mean for emergency physicians?
item.description: Melnick, O'Leary, Zaniello & Abrishamian. American Journal of Emergency Medicine

item.title: Legislative hearing: Health Care Affordability: How to Control Costs in California? (California Assembly Committee on Health)
item.description: Informational hearing at the State Capitol. Glenn Melnick presented two slide decks on health spending and on setting targets (linked from the hearing page). No video is posted on the page.
